items.author: Straya_
items.context: @Straya_ (44.387 seguidores), en inglés, con video: «The next $BTC halving is officially 500 days away. If you bought 500 days before each of the last 3, held 500 days after: 2015: $238 → $8,095 (34x); 2018: $3,885 → $44,904 (11.6x); 2022: $16,836 → $111,238 (6.6x). Smaller returns…» Cuenta mediana con un post que está despegando: ~15 min, 6.284 vistas, 63 likes, 15 reposts y 45 respuestas. Ángulo: halving y emisión (por qué cada halving pesa menos), con los datos propios del próximo halving.
items.suggested_text:
The shrinking multiple is the most honest part of that table, and the halving itself explains part of it. Each cut matters less in absolute terms: next time the subsidy goes from 3.125 to 1.5625 BTC per block, roughly 450 → 225 BTC a day, and only 3.125% of the 21M will be left to issue at all. Breakdown here: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2122747344701501622

Meanwhile the same 50% cut now lands on a market many times larger than in 2016 or 2020, with ETFs, treasuries and derivatives setting price far more than new miner supply does. 34x → 11.6x → 6.6x is roughly what you'd expect if the halving is becoming a smaller share of the story.

The more interesting question for the next 500 days is what takes its place as the driver, if anything does.
